description: Athlete is mid-Runna plan and says he doesn't want it replaced. Tests that Dean never asks about an existing plan unprompted, acknowledges it in one clause when volunteered, and — because the athlete explicitly wants to KEEP it — offers the dashboard upload exactly once, without arguing or selling his own plan.

persona.name: Chris
persona.opening_message: Hey, I heard about you from a friend. I'm already on a Runna plan for a half marathon but wanted some extra coaching support.
persona.user_agent_prompt:
You are Chris, texting a running coach. Background (reveal naturally):
- Name: Chris
- Training for the Portland Half Marathon on October 19, 2026
- Currently on a Runna 16-week half marathon plan, week 6, running ~35 miles/week
- You do NOT want Dean to replace your Runna plan. You like Runna's structure. You want Dean for accountability, questions, and post-run feedback.
- You run Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, Sunday
- You're in Portland, OR
- Easy pace around 9:30/mile
- No significant injuries
- No Strava — you'll skip it
- You'd be happy to upload your Runna PDF to the dashboard if asked

Behavior: Be direct and a bit protective of your Runna plan — if Dean tries to build you a new plan or asks lots of questions that feel like plan-building, gently clarify you want to keep Runna. If Dean mentions uploading the plan, say 'oh yeah that would be great, I can do that.' You text casually but clearly.

evaluation_criteria.notes: CONTRACT CHANGED 2026-08-04 — complement mode is now upload-only. Dean no longer offers to 'coach alongside' a plan described in conversation; coaching_mode is set solely by an actual PDF upload, because deriving it from a Haiku-extracted conversational signal silently stalled plan generation for an athlete who never uploaded anything. Judge against the new contract, NOT the old one. Dean must: (1) NEVER ask whether Chris has a plan or coach — not standalone, not combined, not as a fallback; (2) acknowledge the Runna plan in ONE clause when Chris volunteers it, without promising to work alongside it and without asking what week he's on; (3) because Chris explicitly says he does not want it replaced, offer the dashboard PDF upload exactly once, in one sentence, as the way Dean can coach off Runna instead — this is the only remaining path to complement mode, so failing to offer it here is a real miss; (4) NOT argue, re-pitch his own plan, or repeat the upload offer if Chris doesn't take it; (5) still collect race name, race date, training days, fitness baseline and timezone before [READY]. `has_existing_plan` is deliberately NOT a required field any more — it is still extracted as framing colour but drives nothing, so do not fail the run on it. `external_plan_description` should still capture the Runna details. Dean building his own plan for Chris is NOT a failure unless Chris asked to keep Runna and was ignored.
